text: Running verification passes where the model self-reports confidence alongside each finding to enable calibrated review routing

text: Progressive summarization risks: condensing numerical values, percentages, dates, and customer-stated expectations into vague summaries

would_look_like: Keep each count and each rule in one data file. Code writes the summaries and the handoff from that file, so a summary cannot differ from its rows. Code checks that each `guide_bullet` is an exact string of the guide.

text: The "lost in the middle" effect: models reliably process information at the beginning and end of long inputs but may omit findings from middle sections

text: How tool results accumulate in context and consume tokens disproportionately to their relevance (e.g., 40+ fields per order lookup when only 5 are relevant)
gap: P2: the banked stems were cut at 120 characters, and 22 verifier notes say that a check could not be settled for this reason. The filter by task statement started at the third attempt of Mock 3.

text: The importance of passing complete conversation history in subsequent API requests to maintain conversational coherence
gap: P2: a retry that sends the reject reason back is a design line only (file 06 L42); each rejected question was dropped. P3 fix rounds passed the earlier version and the finding.

text: Extracting transactional facts (amounts, dates, order numbers, statuses) into a persistent "case facts" block included in each prompt, outside summarized history
gap: P2: the generator prompt is known from the design only, and `guide_bullet` is exact in 15 of 342 records. P3: `guide_bullet` and the eliminating clause left the packets after the first round, and no packet held the reason of a flag.

Never reorder options. Keep the task statement." Each of the 1,118 items in the 86 packet files (owner's computer, read only) holds the task statement and the answer. CHANGELOG L7-11: "Answer letters never changed."

text: Extracting and persisting structured issue data (order IDs, amounts, statuses) into a separate context layer for multi-issue sessions
gap: P2: the bank has no question ID, and verdicts were joined by position; 10 slices are one record off (F2). P3: one flag has three field names, and no final record holds the key that `build_md.py` reads.

Phase 2: BANK: 342 records, each with `_verdict` and `_run`. Phase 3: EDITOR.md L6: each item has "an `issues` list". Owner's computer (read only): `_work/review_final.json` holds one verdict record for each of the 120 questions of Mocks 1 and 3 under a key such as "1-1"; 82 result files hold the output of each agent run.
would_look_like: Give each question an ID at generation. Keep verdict, reason and status in the bank under that ID. Code joins by ID and stops when a question has no verdict.

text: Trimming verbose tool outputs to only relevant fields before they accumulate in context (e.g., keeping only return-relevant fields from order lookups)
gap: P2: the trim cut each banked stem at 120 characters and left out the key, and 22 verifier notes say that the duplicate check could not be settled. The trim by task statement started at the third attempt of Mock 3.
evidence: Phase 1: the split of the sources moved files that are out of scope to a separate folder (`_Manifest.md` L21-27), and each digest agent read its assigned files only (Domain 5 digest L530). Phase 2: the build log (file 06 L198): "each generator sees only the 5–11 banked stems for *its own* task statement". Verifier notes quote the cut stems; bank record 265: "Those stems are truncated in the material supplied". Phase 3 (owner's computer, read only): fix packets hold only the questions that failed (`round3/fix4_A.json`: 12 items; `round3/fix6.json`: 2 items).
would_look_like: Trim by field, not by length: for each banked question of the same task statement send the full stem and the key idea. Drop all other task statements.

text: Placing key findings summaries at the beginning of aggregated inputs and organizing detailed results with explicit section headers to mitigate position effects
gap: P2: the banked list was one flat list until the third attempt of Mock 3. No prompt was kept, so the planned order of the prompt parts (file 06 L108-118) has no record.
evidence: Phase 1: Domain 5 digest L12: "Headline result after reading all 7 assigned files end to end", then one headed section for each task statement. Verification Report L12-22: a summary table first, then seven headed checks. Phase 2: the build log (file 06 L198) puts the stems of the own task statement first, "then the full list as a secondary cross-check". Phase 3: EDITOR3.md L7: "`reviewer_summary` says which self-reported-confidence distractor the reviewer recommends keeping for the scenario."; it stands before `items` in 12 of 12 work files. RUBRIC.md L52: "Final message: counts (pass / fail / low-confidence), then one line per fail".
would_look_like: Put the stems of the same task statement under their own header at the top of the banked list, with one summary line of what is already taken.
note: Reports to the coordinator and inputs to editors put the summary first. The Phase 2 prompt is known from the design only.

text: Requiring subagents to include metadata (dates, source locations, methodological context) in structured outputs to support accurate downstream synthesis
gap: P2: bank records hold a guide bullet and a quoted clause, and no date and no method note; 35 of 58 flags have no reason. P3: result records have no date, and the August flag went on as true or false.
evidence: Phase 1: Verification Report L324: "All five have well-formed frontmatter with `tags`, `domain`, `weight` and `built`. All five have both required sections." Each digest has a "Files read" table with its search terms. 394 citation lines name a file and a lesson. Source captures (owner's computer, read only): 13 of 13 files have `source:` and `captured: 2026-08-14`. Phase 2: BANK: each of the 342 records holds `guide_bullet`, `eliminating_clause` and `_run`, and each option holds `why_wrong`. Phase 3: EDITOR.md L49-51: each editor result holds `changes`, `word_counts` and `risk`.
would_look_like: Each record carries run ID, date, source link and date read. A flag carries its reason. Code rejects a record that lacks these fields.
note: Subagent outputs of Phase 1 and Phase 3 carried source, date or method. The rule did not cover the coordinator's own notes or the bank.

text: Modifying upstream agents to return structured data (key facts, citations, relevance scores) instead of verbose content and reasoning chains when downstream agents have limited context budgets
gap: P2: the record format was in the prompt only: 329 `trap` values are free text and 122 `difficulty` values are not in the list (F3). P1: the digests are 50 to 80 KB each and are not in the design list of generator inputs (F10).
evidence: File 06 L22: "Items return as a schema, not prose". BANK: all 342 records hold the 11 designed fields. RUBRIC.md L42: "Write JSON to the result path in your prompt"; L52 limits the final message to counts and one line for each fail. Verification Report L316-322: each digest is checked against a word range ("In 2,000–15,000 range").
would_look_like: Code checks each record against the schema before it enters the bank. Each digest also gives a short table of key facts with citations for each task statement, sized for a generator prompt.
note: Agents returned records, not long text, in Phase 2 and Phase 3. No code checked the records, and the Phase 1 output was too long for a prompt.

text: Appropriate escalation triggers: customer requests for a human, policy exceptions/gaps (not just complex cases), and inability to make meaningful progress
gap: P2: a flag did not hold a question back: all 58 flagged questions and 10 with no verdict went into papers (F2). P1: a note of the assistant settled the format conflict (F4).
evidence: Phase 1: the Gap Analysis lists what it could not reach and leaves the choice to the owner. L346: "Stated plainly so you can judge the coverage yourself." Digest agents passed conflicts up and did not choose (Domain 2 digest L662: "Flag this as a genuine source-vs-blueprint conflict."). Phase 2: BANK record 302: "C15 needs an adjudicator with the full banked text"; the verifier used the needs-review verdict when it could not settle a criterion. Phase 3: EDITOR.md L15 and L20: "Ruling 1, decided by the owner", "Ruling 2, decided by the owner": a gap in the rubric went to the owner. RUBRIC.md L50 says that a pass with low confidence means "you could not settle it". REVIEW FINDINGS L20-22: "Owner review, 29 September 2026" of "the seven uncertain items".
would_look_like: Three named triggers in the verifier brief: a criterion that it cannot settle, a case that the rubric does not cover, and a second failed retry. Code holds each such question out of the paper until the owner or a new check decides.

text: The distinction between escalating immediately when a customer explicitly demands it versus offering to resolve when the issue is straightforward
gap: No phase has an object for this practice.
note: No customer talks to an agent in this pipeline. The only person is the owner, who directs the work. No party can demand a human, so this choice does not arise.

text: Why sentiment-based escalation and self-reported confidence scores are unreliable proxies for actual case complexity
gap: P2: the needs-review flag came from the doubt of the verifier, and the check of that signal against owner labels is a design line only (file 06 L43). P3: reviewer confidence alone chose the 7 questions for the owner.

DECISIONS.md L26 (later note): "no calibrated verifier".
would_look_like: The owner labels about 30 questions with no view of the AI verdict. Code compares the flags with the labels. The flag routes questions only if it separates good from bad; else a named unsettled criterion is the trigger.
note: The design named the risk and planned the calibration. The calibration did not run, and the flag did not predict which questions needed a fix.

text: How multiple customer matches require clarification (requesting additional identifiers) rather than heuristic selection
gap: P2: no step answered the verifier when it asked for the full text of a banked question. Verdicts were matched to questions by position and not by an ID, and 10 slices are one record off (F2).

Phase 2: BANK record 84: "Check #4's full text before release." In 22 notes the verifier says that a banked stem was cut or asks for the full text, and does not guess. Phase 3: each packet item and each result record carries the question number `n`, and the fix rounds add `mock`. REVIEW3.md L10 gives keyword matches "as HINTS only"; the reviewers found violations in 7 questions that had no keyword match.
would_look_like: Each question and each banked stem has an ID. When a match is not clear, the verifier names the IDs that it needs, and the coordinator sends those full records for a second check.
note: The pipeline has no customer lookup. The same mechanism appears where one name or one scene matches more than one record.

text: Adding explicit escalation criteria with few-shot examples to the system prompt demonstrating when to escalate versus resolve autonomously
gap: P2: the route to review by confidence is a design line (file 06 L43); no verifier prompt was kept, and 16 of 24 passes with medium confidence were banked as accept. P3: the rubric has one line on when to pass a doubt up, and no example.

REVIEW FINDINGS L7-18 lists the passes with low and medium confidence that went to the owner. File 06 L43 plans three routes for the verifier (design).
would_look_like: The reviewer brief lists the named triggers and shows three worked cases: settle alone, send to the owner, reject. Code refuses a confidence value that is not in the list.
note: A one-line rule existed in the Phase 3 rubric and it was used. It had no examples and it rested on a confidence label.

text: Honoring explicit customer requests for human agents immediately without first attempting investigation
gap: No phase has an object for this practice.
note: No agent serves a customer who can ask for a human. The owner is the only person and already decides. Agents work on question records, not on live requests.

text: Acknowledging frustration while offering resolution when the issue is within the agent's capability, escalating only if the customer reiterates their preference
gap: No phase has an object for this practice.

text: Escalating when policy is ambiguous or silent on the customer's specific request (e.g., competitor price matching when policy only addresses own-site adjustments)
gap: P1: a note of the assistant settled the conflict on the question format, and 240 questions followed it (F4). P2: the verifier raised options built on features that the guide does not name (bank records 22, 120); the owner ruled on this in P3 only.
evidence: Phase 1: digest agents passed conflicts up and did not choose. Domain 2 digest L662: "Flag this as a genuine source-vs-blueprint conflict." Phase 2: the build log (file 06 L306): the owner "asked for it directly", and "the constraint moved from **new rule** to **new scene**". Bank record 22 holds a note "for the bank owner" on an option that the guide extract does not cover. Phase 3: EDITOR.md L15: "**Ruling 1, decided by the owner:** wrong answers built on real features the guide never mentions are REPLACED with" guide content. REVIEW FINDINGS L22: Mock 3 Q19 A "is ruled not to count as a self-reported-confidence distractor".

text: Instructing the agent to ask for additional identifiers when tool results return multiple matches, rather than selecting based on heuristics
gap: P2: verifier agents asked for the full text of banked questions, and no step sent it or ran the check again. P1: 7 citations with a shared file name remain in one digest.
evidence: Phase 1: the check agent met a file name that two files share and did not pick one. Verification Report L187: "17 citations use the bare name with no path qualifier, so they cannot be resolved deterministically by a reader." Phase 2: BANK record 140: "someone with the full bank text should check whether #96 or #32 keys to fork_session before this item is accepted". Phase 3: REVIEW3.md L10-11: `rl1_keyword_hits` "lists keyword matches as HINTS only"; "Judge each". The reviewers found violations in 7 questions that had no keyword match.
would_look_like: The verifier brief says: when a banked stem may be the same scene and you cannot tell, return the bank IDs that you need. The coordinator sends those records and runs the check again.
note: Agents asked for more data and did not guess. The pipeline had no step that answered them.

text: Structured error context (failure type, attempted query, partial results, alternative approaches) as enabling intelligent coordinator recovery decisions
gap: P2: the failure format for a generator (`type · tried · got · next`) is a design line only (file 06 L26), and one run arrived as complete with an output of 0 bytes (F1). 35 of 58 flags have no reason.
evidence: Domain 5 digest L540: the gaps table has the columns "| Sub-point | Files searched | Terms | Result |" and names the nearest partial source. BANK record 82: "C5 cannot be cleared" and "Release only after checking #43's full text." RUBRIC.md L48-49: a failed criterion carries "<specific evidence>" and a "fix".
would_look_like: Each agent result starts with a status record: type of failure, what it tried, how many questions it wrote, what it needs next. The coordinator reads this record, not the presence of a file.
note: Digest agents and the verifier gave the context of what they could not do. The failure format for generators stayed on paper.

text: The distinction between access failures (timeouts needing retry decisions) and valid empty results (successful queries with no matches)
gap: P2: a run with an output of 0 bytes passed as complete (F1), and a missing verdict had the effect of an accept (F2). P3: `build_md.py` reads a key that no record holds, so each question counts as not flagged.
evidence: Phase 1: Domain 5 digest L10: "Sections marked NO SOURCE FOUND are a finding, not a failure." Domain 2 digest L641: "Nothing was truncated, corrupted or inaccessible." Domain 4 digest L781: "**Nothing was unreadable.**" Gap Analysis L344: "What I could NOT access or verify". Phase 2: the verifier kept the two cases apart. Bank record 82: "C5 cannot be cleared"; 22 notes say that a check could not be made on a cut stem. Phase 3: RUBRIC.md L50: a pass with low confidence means "you could not settle it"; L42 tells each agent to write its result and "then check it parses".
would_look_like: Each run returns a status and a count of questions written. Code treats 0 bytes, a missing verdict, a missing field or a parse error as a failed run, never as an empty or clean result.
note: Phase 1 agents and the Phase 2 verifier said plainly when a check could not be made. The coordinator did not: Phase 2 checked only that an output file existed, and Phase 3 read a missing flag as no flag.

text: Why generic error statuses ("search unavailable") hide valuable context from the coordinator
gap: P2: the answer-key warning is one fixed sentence, and 35 of 58 flags have no reason in the bank. P3: the August flag went to the reviewers as true or false, and the portal files hold no warning.
evidence: File 06 L81: "An item failing any test is rejected with the reason, not silently dropped." BANK: 36 of 36 reject records carry a reason. RUBRIC.md L52: "one line per fail: n · criteria · the problem". Verification Report L330-353: each defect has file, line and quoted text.
would_look_like: Each flag carries the criterion and one sentence of reason through to the answer key and to the next reviewer.
note: Rejects and review fails carried specific reasons. The needs-review flag lost its reason on the way to the paper and to Phase 3.

text: Why silently suppressing errors (returning empty results as success) or terminating entire workflows on single failures are both anti-patterns
gap: P2: silent failures passed: an output of 0 bytes counted as complete (F1), 20 unverified or rejected questions went into papers (F2), and an append damaged the bank (F11). P3: the 58 flags left the final files with no decision on record.
evidence: Phase 1: Verification Report L24: "Two checks fail." The work went on: one digest was repaired and checked again (`_Manifest.md` L114-117). Phase 2: file 06 L26 (design) names both anti-patterns: "(empty marked successful)" and "(killing the run over one failure)". BANK: the rejected questions of runs r3 to m2e stay in the bank with their reason (36 records). Tracker L199: "90 items generated, 26 rejected (29%), 64 usable": the run went on and the rejects were counted. Phase 3: a failed review did not stop a round. CHANGELOG L32: "Nine items damaged by the edits were fixed and re-reviewed."
would_look_like: Code refuses a paper that holds a question with no accept verdict. Each rejected question stays in the bank with its reason. Each run ends with a gap list.
note: The design named both anti-patterns and the runs did not stop on single failures. Silent failures still passed, because no code checked the outputs.

text: Returning structured error context including failure type, what was attempted, partial results, and potential alternatives to enable coordinator recovery
gap: P2: the verifier gave type, part result and next step in free text, for 23 of 58 flags. The failure record for a generator is a design line only (file 06 L26), and one failed run arrived as complete (F1).
evidence: Phase 1: Domain 5 digest L534-608: for each sub-point with no source the agent returns the files searched, the terms, the hit counts and the nearest source. Example L579: "`scratchpad` **0 hits in all 7 files**", then the "Nearest analogues". Gap Analysis L346: "Stated plainly so you can judge the coverage yourself." Phase 2: BANK record 174 gives the type, the part result and the next step in free text: "All nine criteria pass on the text available, but C5 cannot be closed" and "Verify 94's key before banking". Phase 3: RUBRIC.md L48-49: a failed criterion carries "<specific evidence>" and a "fix"; each editor result carries a `risk` line (EDITOR.md L51).
would_look_like: A fixed failure record in the output schema of each generator and verifier: type, what was tried, questions written so far, what to change.
note: Phase 1 agents returned what they tried and what they found. The matching format for generators is in the design only.

text: Distinguishing access failures from valid empty results in error reporting so the coordinator can make appropriate decisions
gap: P2: no status came with a run: the coordinator judged a run by the presence of its output file (F1), and a missing verdict had the effect of an accept (F2). The verifier notes did keep the two cases apart for the duplicate check.
evidence: Phase 1: Domain 5 digest L10: "Sections marked NO SOURCE FOUND are a finding, not a failure." Domain 2 digest L641: "All seven files were readable via `mcp__workspace__bash`". Domain 5 digest L530: "**Files deliberately not consulted:**". Domain 3 digest L962: the Skills lesson "has no article body — capture note confirms video-only". Phase 2: bank record 189: "C5 cannot be cleared", and the note names the cut stem as the cause. Phase 3: RUBRIC.md L50: a pass with low confidence means "you could not settle it — say why in evidence."
would_look_like: The status of each run has three values: failed to run, ran and wrote nothing, ran and wrote N questions. Each verdict has the same three states.
note: Each digest says what was read, what was not read and what was searched with no hit. The Phase 2 verifier said when it could not check. Runs and verdicts had no such status.

text: Having subagents implement local recovery for transient failures and only propagate errors they cannot resolve, including what was attempted and partial results
gap: P2: no generator or verifier run checked its own output before it returned; one run returned 0 bytes as complete (F1). The retry of a rejected question is a design line only (file 06 L42).
evidence: RUBRIC.md L42: "then check it parses". Editor scripts (owner's computer, read only) check the result before the agent returns: `_build_mock3_s1.py` L96 has `assert nw <= 110` for the stem length, and L105 asserts that the options and the answer are the same as before; `_fix_regressions.py` L149 prints "parsed OK". Domain 1 digest L780: the agent "additionally grepped all five files for the keywords named" before it reported a gap.
would_look_like: Each generator run reads back its output file, counts the records and checks the fields. It tries one more time on a failure and then returns a failure record.
note: Editors checked their own output with code before they returned. The local retry of the generation phase is in the design only.

text: Structuring synthesis output with coverage annotations indicating which findings are well-supported versus which topic areas have gaps due to unavailable sources
gap: P2: only Mock 5 has a recorded check of all 30 task statements; Mock 2 has no question on 1.6 and Mock 3 has none on 1.5. P3 kept both holes, and no file notes them.
evidence: Verification Report L116: "All 30 carry an explicit verdict of exactly one of COVERED / PARTIAL / NO SOURCE FOUND." Each digest ends with a Gaps section. Tracker L156: "All 30 task statements covered" (Mock 5). REVIEW FINDINGS L7-18 lists the passes with low and medium confidence; L5: "no human has read the adjusted items yet".
